walkthroughs.body_html:
Research Methods — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Research Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Research Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which cycle has no significant atmospheric phase?
options: Carbon
Nitrogen
Phosphorus
Sulfur

mcqs.q: Average time in a reservoir is called?
options: Flux
Residence time
Lifetime
Half-life

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Because polar bears help spread heat.
They are the same problem.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators have weaker immune systems.

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Anthropogenic perturbation”?
options: Human alteration of natural fluxes (e.g., Haber process doubled global reactive N input).
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.
Slow, sedimentary cycle: weathering of rocks releases phosphate; runs through life and back to ocean sediments.
Compartment storing a quantity of an element, e.g., ocean carbon, soil nitrogen.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Residence time”?
options: Includes volcanic outgassing, biological reduction (DMS) and atmospheric oxidation to sulfate aerosols.
Average time an element spends in a reservoir = reservoir size / flux.
Compartment storing a quantity of an element, e.g., ocean carbon, soil nitrogen.
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reservoir”?
options: Slow, sedimentary cycle: weathering of rocks releases phosphate; runs through life and back to ocean sediments.
Compartment storing a quantity of an element, e.g., ocean carbon, soil nitrogen.
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.
Includes volcanic outgassing, biological reduction (DMS) and atmospheric oxidation to sulfate aerosols.
